articles.content: 40 years ago, the crime drama “ Heat ” opened in France and received positive reviews from Paris critics. No, not the “ Heat ” directed by Michael Mann that starred Robert De Niro and Al Pacino and would go on to become a revered classic — that came nine years later. The “Heat” that played in Europe in 1986 starred Burt Reynolds , was directed by multiple journeyman helmers, and was almost immediately forgotten only months after it limped into U.S. theaters in March of 1987. Film Independent’s New President Wants to Build an L.A. Powerhouse — and Shake Up the Spirit Awards
articles.content: Major change is afoot at Film Independent, the Los Angeles nonprofit that supports indie filmmakers. Not merely a restructuring of departments over the coming years or a revamping of its centerpiece offering, the four-decades-old Spirit Awards , but something more expansive, place-based, and integrated. Since the tragic passing of Josh Welsh, a beloved figure in the indie community who served as Film Independent ’s president for 12 years, many felt a leadership vacuum at a time when the L.A. film industry was in severe crisis, from productions rapidly departing the city to studio mergers. Juan Devis, appointed the new president in April, now envisions Film Independent to become something akin to a nonprofit studio, and equally, a pivotal cultural institution in Los Angeles, to be considered in the same breath as LACMA, the guilds, or the Academy Museum. A day after announcing John Early and Kate Berlant as the new hosts of the Spirit Awards, Devis, in his first public interview since his appointment, spoke to IndieWire about his all-encompassing vision and gave exclusives on the latest promotions following a significant restructuring. Devis’ office sits in the same corner of Film Independent’s headquarters in Miracle Mile as Welsh’s, and though it shares a similar calm, shaped by majestic 270-degree, ninth-story views of the Hollywood Hills to South L.A., Devis has made it bespoke with mementos from his childhood. His father’s paintings circa 1979 hang on the back wall. In Bogotá, Colombia, where he grew up, his father was a painter, his mother a social worker, and Devis a Star Wars buff. articles.content: Living under the pump of graceless digital advertising and toxic social media personalities, it seems like the world has less interest than ever in even bothering to hide the misogyny built into our social order. Most Best Original Song nominees come from popular movies that many Music Branch voters have seen. But every year Diane Warren gets in there. She’s been nominated 17 times and never won. He was 86. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement reads. “He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. He won a Grammy in 1995 and received multiple Emmy, Golden Globe and SAG Award nominations for his work across television and film. In the 2001 New Year Honours list, Queen Elizabeth II appointed Stewart an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE), and in 2010, she knighted him for services to drama. He was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1996. Born July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, West Riding of Yorkshire, England, Stewart left school at 15 to perform in local theater and made his professional stage debut in 1959 at the Theatre Royal, Bristol in a production of Cyrano de Bergerac . Stewart became a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966 and in 1967 made his debut TV appearance on Coronation Street . articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Tyra Banks ’ Smize Productions has tapped Andy Vallentine ( The Mattachine Family ) to direct its Sally Hansen feature film, which Deadline announced was in development last year . In addition to his directing work for Hollywood, Vallentine has a background creating visually bold work for major beauty brands including Sephora and MAC Cosmetics, touts a release from SMiZE Productions. Blending beauty with business intrigue, the film explores how Hansen built one of the industry’s most enduring empires decades before “beauty influencer” was even a phrase — and how her legacy still shapes the $50 billion nail market. articles.content: CBS will broadcast this year’s Kennedy Center Honors , which will be held offsite amid the closure of the main facility. The network’s rights deal for the ceremony expired last year, and is said to have signed a one-year agreement for this year’s ceremony. CBS has broadcast the honors since it started in 1978. The ceremony will be held December 7 at DC’s Capital One Arena, but CBS will air the ceremony on December 27. It also will stream live on Paramount+ Premium. The ceremony will honor Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell . The ceremony will be produced by Den of Thieves, with Jesse Ignjatovic and Evan Prager as executive producers and Barb Bialkowski executive producer and showrunner. Micah Bickham will direct, and Cheche Alara will serve as music producer and music director. Watch on Deadline The center largely ended all major performances ended amid plans to renovate the complex. The plan has been challenged by Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-OH), and a federal judge issued an injunction prohibiting a full-scale closure, albeit center officials have shuttered the main building since September for what they say is for safety reasons. He was 43. Broadway was found dead Tuesday, November 17, in an apartment complex stairwell in Dallas, TX, according to the Dallas County Medical Examiner. The cause of death is pending autopsy results. Broadway made his feature film debut in 2013’s Olympus Has Fallen , the Gerard Butler action film directed by Antoine Fuqua. Broadway went on to appear in several TV series, including Saint George, Kevin From Work, Lucifer, Marvel’s Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Real Husbands of Hollywood. He appeared most recently in two episodes of USA Network’s Colony in 2016-2017. In 2014, Broadway was cast as Commander Linden in the science fiction thriller Teleios , which was later renamed Beyond the Trek , and released in 2017 as a TV movie by Screen Media Films. Broadway’s acting career followed a brief stint in Major League Baseball. As a pitcher for the Chicago White Sox and New York Mets from 2007-09, he compiled a 2-2 record with 5.24 ERA. He was signed by the Toronto Blue Jays as a free agent in 2009 but did not appear in a game for the team.

articles.title: ‘Project 11,’ Shot by 11 Directors in 11 Global Cities, Returns on Oh Short Flips (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.content: “ Project 11 ,” a 2011 survival thriller made by 11 directors working remotely from 11 cities, will be re-released Nov. 26 as the first title under Oh Short Flips ‘ new Classic Shorts vertical. The short pits 11 gamers in 11 cities against one another. Each has 11 minutes to live, and only the final survivor wins. Made years before online phenomena such as the Blue Whale Challenge caused alarm worldwide, the film dealt with fears around deadly real-world gaming dares. Related Stories Disney Expected to Lay Off Thousands of Staffers in Biggest Round of Cuts This Year AI Vocal Modifier Voicemod Inks Disney Deal to Add Star Wars, Marvel Soundboards to Platform Mumbai-based filmmaker Vikas Chandra drove the project, spending months finding 11 directors willing to take part. Their combined crews numbered around 100 people, spread across New York, Los Angeles, Toronto, London, Luxembourg, Tel Aviv, Dar es Salaam, Balochistan, Mumbai, Beijing and Tokyo. The directors could not meet in person. All pre-production and storyboarding happened online. To make actors on different continents look as though they shared a frame, the filmmakers matched eyelines, faked over-the-shoulder setups and found lookalike locations in cities such as London and New York, then tied the footage together through lighting, lens choices and choreography. The film went from script to finished cut in 149 days. A first version running 25 minutes was trimmed to 11 minutes and 11 seconds. Alongside Chandra (Mumbai), the directors are Alessio Giorgetti (New York), Ali Ahmed Brohi (Balochistan), Dharamveer Singh Chauhan (Luxembourg), Ikematsu Hiro (Tokyo), Joseph Cohen (Tel Aviv), Nkumi Mtingwa (Dar es Salaam), Rafal Rakoczy (London), Ryan Singh (Toronto), Sydney Walsh (Los Angeles) and Yi Luo (Beijing). “Long before the AI times, we made ‘Project 11’ with pure HumInt (Human Intelligence) – one part madness, one part ingenuity and a lot of passion, just like the write-ups called it back then,” Chandra said

Broadway was a pitcher who played for the Chicago White Sox and New York Mets. articles.content: Lance Broadway, who pitched in the major leagues with the Chicago White Sox and New York Mets before becoming an actor, has died. He was 43. Broadway died Tuesday, according to a reporter for the Texas Christian University sports website HornedFrogBlitz.com (he pitched for the school in 2005). articles.content: Wicker ‘ s filmmaking team is relishing its viral moments and box office success — not to mention its horny memes . During a screening of Wicker at Toruń Camerimage Film Festival in Poland on Thursday, cinematographer Lol Crawley introduced the movie and expressed appreciation for it having become a social media sensation. Olivia Colman stars in directors Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer’s romantic fantasy as a lonely woman who commissions a basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to create a husband ( Alexander Skarsgard ) for her. articles.content: NBC is making a big change for Broadway performers in this year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. Rather than featuring individual performances, the telecast has gathered nine Broadway shows to sing a 10-minute medley at the top of the show created for this year’s parade, which is Macy’s 100th. The shows participating in the medley include several long-runners, in the case of Wicked , Chicago , Hamilton , The Book of Mormon and Aladdin, as well as Schmigadoon! and The Lost Boys , new musicals that both opened last season. The performances air on Peacock and NBC at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. The change opens up performing on the telecast to more shows than usual, with last year’s parade only featuring three Broadway shows. It also shines a light on the long-runners, which is atypical as the performance is typically used to highlight shows that opened within the prior season. articles.title: Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation
articles.summary: "Wildwood" director Travis Knight and "Tangles" director Leah Nelson tell IndieWire how they helped shape vocal performances for animation.
articles.content: Film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet. Voice acting in animation is a discipline in its own right — as legends like Mel Blanc and Eric Bauza show — where actors impart a kind of electric energy that carries through into the art style of what they’re voicing. So is voice directing. And the secret to both is in providing foundations for animators to build something bigger. “ Wildwood ” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not. There isn’t the same kind of immersiveness for actors that live-action sets, costumes, and the basic pleasure of getting to read lines against other actors all provide. They have to build it from scratch. articles.content: When you hire a 20-year-old director to adapt his own viral YouTube series into a major Hollywood film , you’re not going to end up with a traditional movie. That’s part of what made Kane Parsons’ “ Backrooms ” such a massive critical and commercial success for A24 . Audiences were eager to embrace Parsons as a major new filmmaking voice — and his crew members were just as excited for the chance to work with him. During IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, “Backrooms” VFX Supervisor Edward Douglas broke down the unique workflow that he developed with Parsons during pre-production. He explained that Parsons was used to making his own effects in Blender, so the team started communicating with him using the popular VFX software. Related Stories Aaron Pierre on ‘Lanterns,’ the DC Shake-Up, and Landing a Role in Ryan Gosling’s ‘Star Wars’ Movie Director Brian Duffield Had to Find a New Form of Visual Storytelling for ‘Whalefall’ “The first conversation I had with Kane Parsons was ‘How do you like to work?’ And we embraced his process,” Douglas said. “Because his way of communicating with the entire crew was first, through Blender. articles.title: Director Brian Duffield Had to Find a New Form of Visual Storytelling for ‘Whalefall’
articles.summary: Director Brian Duffield talks about the logistical and aesthetic challenges of telling a story that takes place almost entirely inside a whale's stomach.
articles.content: Director Brian Duffield is a cinephile who watches a lot of movies, but when the time came to direct his adventure film “ Whalefall ” he was dismayed to realize he couldn’t think of a single film he could look to as a model. “It was a nightmare for that reason,” Duffield told IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit podcast . “It also the joy of it, having a room full of amazingly gifted artists all starting from this place of real befuddlement.” In the movie, Austin Abrams plays a scuba diver who gets swallowed by a sperm whale and has only an hour of oxygen to keep him alive while he tries to escape; it’s a premise that posed multiple challenges for Duffield and his team, starting with the question of how exactly to build the stomach that Abrams would be trapped inside for the majority of the film — and how to shoot those scenes. articles.title: Ryan Coogler’s Proximity Media Hires Former Netflix Exec Tendo Nagenda as President
articles.summary: The exec behind "Da 5 Bloods," "Glass Onion," and "Ma Rainey's Black Bottom" will oversee all of Proximity's creative divisions.
articles.content: Tendo Nagenda , a former executive on Netflix’s film team, has been tapped as president of Proximity Media , the production company founded by Ryan Coogler , Zinzi Coogler, and Sev Ohanian, the founders announced Thursday. Nagenda spent four years at Netflix under film chief Scott Stuber, exiting in 2022, and in that time he shepherded films like Spike Lee’s “Da 5 Bloods,” “The Old Guard,” “Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom,” “The Harder They Fall,” and “Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery.” Nagenda will oversee all aspects of creative development and production at Proximity, including its film, TV, and non-fiction divisions, and will report directly to the founders. The heads of Film, Television and Nonfiction will all report directly to Nagenda, and he’ll work alongside marketing and operations lead Terra Potts and music lead Ludwig Göransson. He starts on November 30. articles.title: Why the Radical Lesbian Filmmaker Doc ‘Barbara Forever’ Deserves Oscar Recognition
articles.summary: IndieWire talks to director Brydie O'Connor about her expansive, empathetic, Sundance-winning archival portrait of pioneering lesbian filmmaker Barbara Hammer.
articles.content: Finally, a documentary as radical as the lesbian avant-garde feminist filmmaker it’s about. First-time feature filmmaker Brydie O’Connor’s Sundance-winning documentary “ Barbara Forever ” is a hypnotic archival collage that retraces the life, work, and death of Barbara Hammer. The documentary, an early fall Strand release produced in partnership with Pamela Koffler and Christine Vachon’s recently Oscar-winning Killer Films , won in Park City for Matt Hixon’s editing. (Kristen Stewart also jumped on board as an executive producer.) It’s not hard to see why. “ Barbara Forever ” is an archival documentary that unfolds in the shape and style of its subject, an experimental filmmaker who put together some of the first publicly projected lesbian erotica actually made by a lesbian. Voiceover by the filmmaker spans her early career in the Bay Area (and halcyon days as an out lesbian), her 1992 feature debut “Nitrate Kisses,” and the final years of a cancer battle that ended in 2019. articles.title: ‘The Gilded Age’ Renewed for Fifth Season Following Ratings Boom
articles.summary: The HBO series, beloved for its opulence and pageantry, is coming off its most-watched season.
articles.content: Fans of “The Gilded Age,” rejoice! There are still more luncheons to plan, more balls to savor, and more opera opening nights to fight over. Yes, the HBO original series has been renewed for a fifth season. The move follows a surge in popularity that began with the show’s drama-filled third season , which saw Bertha (Carrie Coon) and George Russell’s (Morgan Spector) relationship strain, and has continued with the fourth season, which has dealt with their marriage troubles, the wedding of Peggy Scott (Denée Benton), and a visit from Grover Cleveland. Clearly, it’s working. Viewership for Season 4 has grown week over week, HBO stated in a press release. Episode 3 hit a season high of 4.3 million U.S. cross-platform viewers and episodes are averaging 5.9 million viewers and growing. That outpaces the prior season by nearly 20 percent. Bringing 19th-century high-society to life is expensive, and the show initially struggled to become a ratings powerhouse despite being co-created by Julian Fellowes of “Downton Abbey” fame. In interviews, the cast admitted that they often feared they would be canceled. But audiences have shown up in a big way, and Fellowes and his co-creator Sonja Warfield recently told IndieWire that they have more stories to tell beyond this season. “We have a Season 5 in us if we’re allowed to do it,” Fellowes said. “But when you write a TV series, you have to finish every season so that it could be the end, because one day it will be.” In its three eligible seasons, “The Gilded Age” has earned 15 total Emmy nominations, including Outstanding Drama Series and Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series, as well as a Screen Actors Guild Award

articles.title: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Review: David Fincher’s Breezy Tarantino Spinoff Is a Disappointing Compromise Between Great Directors
articles.summary: Hollywood's chillest stuntman returns in Netflix's fun but muddled "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" follow-up.
articles.content: The scratchy “vintage” Netflix logo says everything so well that the rest of the movie almost feels like it’s belaboring the point: “ The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth ” is a story about a town where half the people are dreaming up the future, the other half are desperate to mythologize the past, and all of them are stuck together in the ugly compromise we call the right fucking now. Then again, “story” might be too strong a word for the unbothered zen noir that Quentin Tarantino has spun off from his 1969-set hit “ Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, ” which memorably ended with former TV Western star Rick Dalton and his longtime stuntman Cliff Booth saving Manson Family victim Sharon Tate from the cruel fate that befell her in real life. Los Angeles was built on the promise that history could be rewritten, and that anyone who made their way onto a studio lot could print the legend, but the present is another beast altogether. It’s feral. Unforgiving. It has to be survived before it can be shaped into a story worth telling, even if that isn’t much of a story at all.
